headline: S&P 500 futures: leveraged funds at their most net-long of the year, asset managers near their least.
stands_out: Data: the S&P 500 rose 1.41% over the week to 6,612.40, led by technology (XLK +3.22%) and discretionary (XLY +2.15%); energy (XLE) fell 2.59%. In the Sep 8 futures report leveraged funds sat at the 100th percentile and asset managers at the 2nd, both crowded. Bull side: SPY took in $4.1B from Sep 5. Bear side: the Russell 2000 slipped 0.66% and equal-weight trailed cap-weight by 1.84 points over a month, so breadth is narrow.
look_into: [Positioning](pos-card): 10-year note futures show asset managers at their largest net long of the year and leveraged funds at their largest net short. [Sectors](sec-card): technology leads on price while leveraged funds sit near a one-year low in technology futures. [Cash](cash-card): retail money funds held $3,009.0B on Aug 3, down $35.7B over 13 weeks, which may be cash moving into risk.
chart_note: Two of the four trader classes sat at opposite ends of their year in the Sep 8 report.
